promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the assessment objectives.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What two emaciated children does the Ghost of Christmas Present reveal beneath his robe?
questions.explain: The children Ignorance and Want symbolise the dangers of neglecting the poor.

questions.q: In an allegory, characters and events...
options: Are described in great factual detail
Stand symbolically for wider ideas or moral/political meanings
questions.explain: An allegory works on two levels: the literal story carries a deeper symbolic or moral meaning.

questions.q: The play is set in 1912 but was written in 1945. What does Priestley use this gap to comment on?
options: The two World Wars and the need for social change
questions.explain: Writing after two world wars, Priestley contrasts Birling's complacency with the lessons of conflict.

questions.q: Which Victorian theory, holding that helping the poor only increased their numbers, does Scrooge's early attitude echo?
questions.explain: Scrooge's line about "decrease the surplus population" reflects Malthusian thinking Dickens criticised.

questions.q: How did Mrs Birling contribute to Eva Smith's death?
options: She sacked her from a shop
She used her influence to deny Eva help from a charity
She gave her too much money
questions.explain: As head of a charity, Mrs Birling refused the pregnant Eva assistance and blamed the father.

questions.q: At the start of A Christmas Carol, how is Scrooge described?
options: A cold, miserly and unfeeling man
questions.explain: Scrooge is "a squeezing, wrenching, grasping, scraping, clutching, covetous old sinner".

questions.q: What does Inspector Goole warn will happen if people do not learn the lesson of responsibility?
options: They will be taught it "in fire and blood and anguish"
questions.explain: His final speech warns that ignoring social responsibility leads to suffering "in fire and blood and anguish".

questions.q: By the end of the novella, how is Scrooge changed in relation to Tiny Tim?
options: He sends him to a workhouse
He becomes "a second father" to Tiny Tim
questions.explain: Dickens writes that to Tiny Tim, who did not die, Scrooge "was a second father".

questions.q: Who is the first spirit to visit Scrooge, warning him of his fate?
questions.explain: Marley, Scrooge's dead business partner, appears bound in chains he "forged in life".

options: The audience knows something a character does not
Two characters say the same line
questions.explain: Dramatic irony arises from the gap between the audience's knowledge and a character's ignorance, creating tension or poignancy.

options: A stanza of exactly four lines
questions.explain: Blank verse is unrhymed lines of iambic pentameter, much used by Shakespeare for noble characters.

questions.q: What unsettling twist occurs at the very end of the play?
options: A phone call announces a real inspector is coming to investigate a girl's death
questions.explain: After doubting Goole was real, the family learns a girl has died and a police inspector is on his way.
